observations: A figure with several splayed limbs fills most of the frame, arms raised and splayed outward, built from dense overlapping loops of white, yellow, red, blue, and black line against a grey wave-patterned background.
The face is the darkest zone: two large square eye sockets hold concentric rings of red, yellow, and white, and a tooth-filled mouth shows a row of sharp white teeth outlined heavily in black.
A cast shadow falls directly behind the figure onto the grey background, and a faint red partial arc is visible in the upper right corner, partially obscured by the dark edge.
reading: The figure throws its limbs outward in all directions, and the tangled lines building its body feel loose and agitated against the smoother grey waves behind it. The face anchors the chaos: squared eye sockets and an open-toothed mouth read as alarm or a shout. The shadow doubles the form without repeating its color, adding a quieter second presence beneath the noise.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors #46 and #48. Compared to those two, #47 layers more line colors across the body and is the only one of the three to use a cast shadow as a structural element.

connections.reason: nnxyz nnotb #46 shares the raised-arm pose and toothed open mouth, but its lines are sparser and darker against a flat teal ground, making the contrast with #47's pale multi-color density direct and visible.
nnxyz nnotb #27 centers a wide-mouthed figure with red-ringed eyes on a grey blurred background, offering a close formal parallel to #47's face structure despite the very different body treatment.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye settle first — on the open mouth, the splayed hands, or the shadow — and what does that order suggest about how the lines direct attention across the image?
ambiguities: The partial red arc in the upper right corner is not clearly resolved as a separate drawn element or a background layer bleed.
nnxyz nnotb #48 uses scattered dots and smooth color fields with no structural parallel to #47, so it was excluded from connections.
